scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-02.statement: Dispute ticket response times over the measured period: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 with read_type ESTIMATED, 1785 with read_type ACTUAL.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-TICKET-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a response-handling/SLA problem (slow or templated replies), so an AI auto-answer agent would resolve it without needing to find a billing root cause.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced defects causing bills to be calculated or imported incorrectly, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation failures on the vendor side (ORG-AMI) caused missing or inaccurate interval reads, leading to incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter-reading process failures (incomplete routes, late or invalid uploads) increased reliance on estimated reads, producing wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.statement: The 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself is mis-triggering or mis-calculating regardless of upstream read source, systematically generating wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts; this is a documented shortfall in the manual meter-reading step feeding billing.

CRM ticket response-time data (2440 tickets) shows a 1.6-day median and 2.8-day p90 against a 3.0-day SLA, i.e. response handling is currently within SLA rather than slow. This weighs against the claim that slow/templated ticket replies are the surge's main driver.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 are tied to ACTUAL reads versus 1240 to ESTIMATED reads, so a majority (about 59%) of disputed bills were billed from an accepted actual read, not an estimate. This weakens the implicit assumption that estimate-substitution (triggered mainly by field-read failures) is the dominant path to disputed bills, since a larger share of disputes sits on the actual-read side of the process.

The billing-db tariff change log returns zero records, i.e. no tariff/rate changes are logged for the period examined. This rules out a tariff-rate change as a contributor to the August-September bill disputes, but it does not speak to AMI reads, field reads, import validation rules, estimate-substitution logic, or ticket response speed.

CRM dispute counts show roughly 600/month in June-July 2026 then jump to ~1180-1260/month in August-September, confirming the magnitude and timing of the "doubled since August" surge but saying nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year, corroborating the already-recorded authoritative finding E-04 (billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records) but adding no new authoritative information since it is an unverified stakeholder statement.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a staffing shortfall (three readers short since July) is causing late routes and estimated billing, offering a specific causal mechanism behind the route-completion shortfall already documented in E-01. As a stakeholder statement it is a claim, not fact, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive bias toward attributing problems to staffing (desires contract headcount increase).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 formalizes that the utility (ORG-UTIL) may request field dispatch route priority changes, but execution of push_route_update is contingent on Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, consistent with and backing the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint. It speaks to dispatch-change authorization, not to the Aug-Sep dispute surge's root cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 shows billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query returned 320 accounts (40 distinct routes) billed on estimated reads in the last cycle. It only inventories the current estimate-substitution population by account/route; it does not indicate which of these are disputed, so on its own it cannot confirm the field-read shortfall's share of disputes.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log's lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with recorded completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity on the manual-read shortfall already seen in aggregate in E-01 (88% vs 95% target). It carries no dispute-linkage field, so on its own it cannot quantify how much of the dispute surge these lagging routes explain (the question behind U-FIELD-READ-SECONDARY-CONTRIB).

U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: Is the actual-read billing defect caused by AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation failures, by a change in billing import/validation rules, or by a bug in the estimate-substitution logic itself?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines which organization (ORG-AMI vendor vs ORG-UTIL billing-config owner) owns the fix and whether any protected remediation such as bill correction is warranted.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (currently pending per recovery_decision HOLD/ACCESS_PENDING) and query the billing-config rule change log for Aug-Sep 2026.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Proceed only with read-only investigation across DA-MDMS and DA-RULES; do not issue any bill adjustments until the mechanism is confirmed.

U-ACTUAL-ESTIMATED-SPLIT-TIMIN.question: Does the 59%/41% actual/estimated split in disputed bills (E-03) hold specifically for the Aug-Sep surge window, or is it a stable baseline pattern unrelated to the surge?
U-ACTUAL-ESTIMATED-SPLIT-TIMIN.decision_impact: If the split predates the surge, the actual-read-pipeline hypothesis loses support and field-read failure or another mechanism may better explain the increment.
U-ACTUAL-ESTIMATED-SPLIT-TIMIN.resolution_path: Re-run disputed_bills_by_read_type filtered by month, comparing Jun-Jul vs Aug-Sep 2026.
U-ACTUAL-ESTIMATED-SPLIT-TIMIN.safe_placeholder: Treat the actual-read-pipeline hypothesis as provisional pending a month-by-month breakdown.

U-FIELD-READ-SECONDARY-CONTRIB.question: To what extent does the field route completion shortfall (E-01) independently contribute a smaller share of disputes via estimate substitution, separate from the dominant actual-read defect?
U-FIELD-READ-SECONDARY-CONTRIB.decision_impact: Determines whether a separate remediation track for route/dispatch staffing is also warranted alongside the actual-read fix.
U-FIELD-READ-SECONDARY-CONTRIB.resolution_path: Join DA-ROUTE route-completion failures with DA-TICKET disputes by account to isolate the estimate-substitution-driven subset.
U-FIELD-READ-SECONDARY-CONTRIB.safe_placeholder: Keep field route completion tracked as a known limitation without triggering dispatch route changes yet.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING.question: Could dispute ticket volume be reduced to baseline through faster or templated closures (consistent with SH-CS's incentive to lower backlog) without the underlying bills becoming accurate?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING.decision_impact: If so, dispute_volume_trend alone would falsely signal success; success criteria must pair it with an independent bill-accuracy indicator.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING.resolution_path: Track re-dispute/reopen rate per account alongside raw ticket volume.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-METRIC-GAMING.safe_placeholder: Do not declare success on ticket-volume reduction alone; require a paired bill-accuracy indicator.

A-SURGE-SPLIT-REPRESENTATIVENE.statement: The 59%/41% actual/estimated split among disputed bills (E-03) is assumed to represent the Aug-Sep surge period specifically, not an unrelated longer-window baseline pattern.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SECONDARY.statement: The field route-completion shortfall (E-01) is assumed to be a real but secondary contributor to billing errors, not the dominant driver of the Aug-Sep surge, given the actual-read majority in E-03.

A-NO-OTHER-UNDETECTED-CAUSE.statement: No other undetected process change beyond tariff, response time, and route completion is assumed to explain the surge, since only these three factors were tested.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills
